payload.goal: Every iteration runs in its own worktree and branch BY DEFAULT, proven live end-to-end through the server and board, and carries a local machine seeded from systematic and trimmed in place - completing i5's blessed goal and fixing the two shipped defects.
payload.pulled_in:
From the two i5 defects:
- Default branching (note-e8a12b600638): remove the opt-in - every se_loop_start provisions iter/<iteration> in .worktrees/, keeping ONLY the legitimate never-nest guard (a worktree-resident loop starts plain). Restores i5's blessed goal ('each runs in its own worktree and branch').
- Live routing, proven (note-6815f9db4930): the running server/board must FIND and drive an open iteration wherever its worktree lives (openInstance must span the worktree homes, not just the server's own root) - proven by an end-to-end test that opens, walks, gates and ships an iteration INSIDE its worktree through the real tool surface.
From the owner ruling (present, this session):
- Local seed-then-trim machines: an iteration carries its OWN top-level machine, seeded from systematic and trimmed locally in its branch (today only sub-machines can be iteration-local; the top-level machine is shared by-name). This is the machinery the owner OK'd, and it makes future refine cuts clean.
From the retro process-stale finding:
- A validation guard for i5b's own goal: M8 Validate traces the blessed goal + plan steps to a passing LIVE (end-to-end) test - so 'shipped but never run for real' cannot recur here (the GENERAL guard is the next-retro deep dive).

payload.rigor: Systematic, unpruned, and deliberately HEAVY on prove + validate - this iteration exists to fix a validation regression, so it must not repeat it. M6 Prove burns the real unknown FIRST: does an iteration actually run live in its worktree through the server/board (the routing probe the owner wants before we trust it)? M7 Build lands default provisioning + live routing + local seed-trim machines. M8 Validate is the crux: an END-TO-END/LIVE test that opens, walks, gates and ships an iteration inside its own worktree through the real tools - unit-green is explicitly NOT acceptance here - and i5b's blessed goal traces to that live test. NO strikes: a reuse-style reduction would be exactly the corner-cutting that produced the defect. i5b runs on trunk (bootstrap - it builds the very branching it will hand to future iterations); the owner blesses each gate (attended, not delegated).
